2314.closed: The plaintext is in the volume for the cipher seen, though one link is inferred, not decoded. (1) The digit runs inside the letters on 14, 18 and 22 have their plaintext in the clear line written beneath or between the digit lines. The run 447.168.374.(268|507).380.(336|622).384(.325) comes with the word 'fredspresenter(ne)' in that clear line in four places: 14 left (cipher '447168374268380336384406...' over 'fredspresenter som af fregatten Hercules lossade', then '439757217...' over 'blefwit, som war under den 15 April'); 14 right ('...157447168374' over 'resterande fredspresenterne och om Doniers foervaerfvande'); 18 ('4471683745073806223843...' over 'presenterne, nu mer aen en maanads'); 22 left ('168,374,507,380,622,...' with 'hu dess de ... freds presenter und hwad' between the digit lines). So these lines are the plaintext of the digits, not separate text, and the lead's 'crib' is a decipherment. (2) The long cipher letter on 11-13 opens in clear ('Till underdaanigst efterlefnad af Edr Exc:s Herr Rikst. etc.'), then has about 75 rows of run-together digits, received 'ank. d. 8 augusti'. Images 7-10 are a clear letter that opens with the same words ('Till underdaanigst efterlefnad af Eders Excellences ...'), has the same receipt note 'ank. d. 8 Aug.', is about as long, and ends 'Ed. Ex:s tit. / Salee den 21 April 1764' with no signature, the form of a copy. So 7-10 is very probably the plaintext of 11-13, but no line of 11-13 has been decoded against it. What is left: decode a row of 11 against 7 using the pairs from 14, 18 and 22; if it fits, the volume is read in full.
